# AMD Patch for Voxy v1.0.1 Update

**Minecraft 26.1.2 | Fabric Loader 0.19.2 | Java 25**

## What's New

This release marks a full rewrite of the patch on top of the official Fabric 1.21.11+ (26.1.2) template.

- **Primary fix:** `HierarchicalOcclusionTraverserMixin` now intercepts the HiZ traversal compute shader at the exact moment Voxy assembles it (after all `#import` directives are resolved), injecting the AMD-safe depth clamp before compilation.
- **Fallback:** `ShaderLoaderMixin` remains as a safety net in case Voxy ever refactors its shader loading pipeline.
- **Startup crash bypass:** `CapabilitiesMixin` still prevents the infamous `IllegalStateException("it bork, amd is bork")` on Polaris GPUs.
- **Maintenance:** All patch constants have been centralized into `ShaderPatchUtil` so future updates only require editing a single file.
- **Artifacts:** JARs now include the Minecraft version in their name (e.g., `amd-patch-for-voxy-1.0.1-mc26.1.2.jar`) to avoid confusion between builds.

---

## TL;DR -- Where I've Been

I owe everyone who starred, commented, or tried to contribute an explanation for the long silence.

First, the honest part: I am still going through a prolonged period of unemployment, depression, and financial hardship. When you're in that headspace, you tend to withdraw from everything and everyone. I ended up isolating myself, which meant I also left behind people who were genuinely interested in helping develop this patch. That was unfair to them, and I'm sorry.

On top of that, I personally felt that trying to engage with the original mod's community spaces became increasingly difficult. I experienced a lot of my AMD-related bug reports and threads being removed, including ones where players were simply trying to troubleshoot problems together. Over time, I felt like my work on this patch was being ignored and devalued explicitly because I used AI as a tool to help me code. It wasn't seen as a legitimate approach, even though I was working full-time as a video editor at an agency and had very little free time. AI was a necessity for me to make any progress at all, not a shortcut to avoid learning.

That hostility, combined with the fact that I was already burned out from working full-time as a video editor at an agency, left no energy left to navigate those spaces.

I won't promise a grand comeback. What I can say is that I'll try to move forward in small steps, as my situation allows: back-porting this patch to the most popular modpack versions, working through the open issues, reaching out to Brazilian content creators who might find it useful, and maybe, eventually, building a small, independent community around the patch where people can actually get help without fear of being shut down.

To be completely transparent: just coming back to work on this project and writing this right now is giving me a mild panic attack. My heart is racing, my arms and legs are shaking, and I'm very scared. But I'm doing it anyway.

Thank you for your patience.
